The reported 'Wires & Cables' segment splits into Cables and Raw Material (the copper-rod pass-through arm) and the two sum exactly to it. Turnkey gross profit is taken from the income statement where it differs marginally from the workbook

vol_hist.source: Disclosed sales volumes: cables in tonnes, meters in units, transformers in MVA (company earnings releases, FY2024 with FY2023 comparatives). These reproduce the disclosed gross profit per tonne (90,020 / 119,043), per meter (418 / 707) and per MVA (136,345 / 221,065) exactly

q1_units.source: Q1-2025 disclosed volumes with Q1-2024 comparatives (Q1-2025 earnings release): cables 41,476t (-7.8%), meters 1,169,502 (+44.1%), transformers 5,112 MVA (-0.6%). Used with the FY2024 seasonal share to estimate the FY2025 volume base, which is not itself disclosed

copper_hist.source: LME copper cash, annual average USD/tonne (house commodity reference)

fx_hist.source: Annual average USD/EGP. The audited FY2024 note discloses closing 50.91 / average 43.96 for 2024 and closing 30.96 / average 30.59 for 2023; the figures here are the house averages consistent with those disclosures

fx_path.source: USD/EGP average-rate path, about 6%/yr of depreciation from the FY2025 average of 49.5. This is a genuine driver in the bottom-up build, not a translation convenience: copper is priced in dollars, so it sets the Egyptian-pound price per tonne of cable and rod directly. DELIBERATELY BELOW covered-interest parity, which on the 22.31% pound against a ~4.3% dollar rate implies about 17%/yr — the base case assumes disinflation closes most of that gap rather than the currency absorbing it. The parity case is carried as an explicit sensitivity

copper_fcst.source: LME copper. FY2026 is set at USD 13,400/t, between the Q1-2026 average of 12,852 actually realised and the current cash price of about 14,000 (13.9-14.2k, early August 2026); thereafter the current level is held flat. Held flat rather than forecast: copper is the largest single input and a directional view on it would dominate the valuation. The -10% column of the sensitivity carries the mean-reversion case

cables_vol_growth.source: Cable tonnage growth. The FY2025 base is a 7.7% volume DECLINE on FY2024 (disclosed Q1-2025 -7.8%), so the forecast is a recovery to roughly the FY2024 level by FY2028 and modest growth thereafter, supported by regional grid build-out, data-centre demand and the export book. No capacity step-change is assumed

cables_uplift.source: Fabrication uplift: cable price per tonne divided by the copper cost per tonne. History back-solves to 1.386 (FY2023) and 1.261 (FY2024); the forecast is held at 1.30, between the two. This is the term that converts a copper price into a cable price, and holding it flat means no pricing-power assumption is being smuggled in

cables_gp_t_fy25.source: Cable gross profit per tonne, Q1-2025 as disclosed (against 93,672 in Q1-2024 on the restated basis). Taken as the FY2025 run-rate: it is the hard evidence for how far cable conversion margins actually compressed, and it is what pins the FY2025 unit build to reality rather than to an assumption

cables_conv.source: Cable conversion margin — gross profit as a share of the realised price per tonne — for the forecast years. History back-solves to 25.0% (FY2023), 22.8% (FY2024) and roughly 13.8% (FY2025, from the disclosed gross profit per tonne against the back-solved price per tonne). The forecast recovers only part of that collapse and never approaches the FY2023-24 levels, which carried devaluation gains on cheaply bought copper inventory

unit_gp_growth.source: Growth in gross profit PER UNIT for the manufacturing lines — per tonne of cable and rod, per MVA of transformer, per meter. This is the correct structure for a converter: when copper spikes, revenue rises because the metal is passed through, but the conversion margin earned on each tonne does not, so the percentage margin falls. Modelling these as a percentage of a copper-inflated price would manufacture profit out of a commodity move. The path is set at roughly Egyptian cost inflation, i.e. a flat real conversion margin with no recovery in unit profitability assumed

margin_recovery.source: Recovery factor applied to the FY2025 gross margins of the non-cable lines. FY2025 margins are calibrated to the disclosed group gross profit, which implies roughly a 10% compression against FY2024 across those lines; the forecast recovers about half of it by FY2030 and no more

rawmat_vol_growth.source: Raw-material (copper rod) tonnage growth. This arm is close to a pure pass-through: implied volume was 99kt in FY2023 and 120kt in FY2024

rawmat_uplift.source: Raw-material price per tonne as a multiple of the copper cost — a thin conversion spread over the metal

rawmat_gp.source: Raw-material gross margin. History 13.4% (FY2023), 15.4% (FY2024); the forecast is struck at the lower end

ec_backlog.source: Engineering and construction order book: USD 6.5bn translated at the spot rate. Disclosed as 'approximately USD 6.5bn, above the group's typical historical range'. The reported turnkey backlog was EGP 165bn (Mar-2024), 239bn (Jun-2024) and 196bn (Dec-2024), so the current book is a genuine step up

ec_burn.source: Share of the opening order book converted to revenue each year. The FY2025 revenue of roughly EGP 88bn against a book of EGP 324bn implies about 27%, i.e. a three-and-a-half-year book. The rate is tapered as the book lengthens

ec_book_to_bill.source: New awards as a multiple of revenue recognised. Above one early, reflecting the disclosed step up in the order book, converging to replacement

seg_rev_fy25_disclosed.source: FY2025 segment revenue on the restated five-segment taxonomy: engineering & construction 87,100.7, electrical products 17,703.5, digital solutions 16,594.1, infrastructure investment 3,857.9, with wires, cables & accessories 155,792.9 - summing to the reported 281,049. REPLACES the earlier assumption that the FY2024 mix carried forward, which an external audit correctly identified as the prior year's mix relabelled. TWO competing external claims were tested against each other: press coverage of the release reports E&C growth of +51%, which would put the segment at 105,764. That figure is REJECTED because it fails an independent coherence test - it leaves so little revenue for cables that the implied fabrication uplift over copper falls to 1.077, below anything in the company's own history (1.386 in FY2023, 1.261 in FY2024). The 87,100.7 figure (+24.4%) passes that test, and is adopted on that basis rather than on the authority of either source

ec_gp.source: Engineering and construction gross margin. History 11.6% (FY2023) and 11.2% (FY2024); held at 11.0%

transformers_vol_growth.source: Transformer MVA growth. History: 14,521 MVA (FY2023) to 17,619 (FY2024), +21.3%, then broadly flat through Q1-2025. Regional transmission investment supports mid-single-digit growth

transformers_gp.source: Transformer gross margin as a share of price per MVA. History 29.9% (FY2023) and 34.4% (FY2024); struck between them

meters_vol_growth.source: Smart-meter unit growth. Volumes fell 5.1% in FY2024 but Q1-2025 ran +44.1% y/y as national metering programmes restarted

meters_gp.source: Meter gross margin as a share of price per unit. History 23.9% (FY2023) and 27.2% (FY2024)

unit_price_inflation.source: Nominal price growth for the units not priced off copper (meters). Set below Egyptian headline inflation on the disinflation path

other_growth.source: Revenue growth for the two smallest lines — other electrical products, and infrastructure investment (industrial development, logistics, utilities, dry port and independent power projects). Together under 3% of revenue

other_gp.source: Gross margins on the two residual lines. History: other electrical products 53.9% (FY2023) and 50.7% (FY2024); infrastructure 50.7% and 61.8%. Struck conservatively

opex_pct.source: The net operating load between gross profit and EBITDA, as a share of revenue — selling, general and administrative costs and other expenses, less other income. History: 5.94% (FY2023) and 5.30% (FY2024). FY2025 solves to a much lower level, so the forecast glides back TOWARD the historical norm rather than assuming the FY2025 load persists. This is the single most conservative choice in the rebuild

foreign_share_fy25.source: 'Over 70% of revenues generated abroad' (company 2025 commentary). Used to report the currency split of the bottom-up revenue build, and to translate the copper-linked lines, which are dollar-priced by construction

nwc_pct.source: Net working capital as a share of revenue, held flat at the historical level. Computed from the audited balance sheets: FY2023 24.1% and FY2024 23.1% (inventories + contract assets + receivables less payables less contract liabilities). This is the single largest cash-flow driver in the model

capex_pct.source: Capex as a share of revenue, tapering. History: FY2023 3.2%, FY2024 3.8% (a capacity burst — property, plant and equipment rose 53% in one year), Q1-2025 4.7% annualised. The taper assumes the current expansion cycle completes and spending settles toward maintenance plus modest capacity addition

dna_pct.source: Depreciation and amortisation as a share of revenue. History: FY2024 0.97%, Q1-2025 1.15%; set at 1.05% rising with the enlarged asset base

rf.source: Egypt 10-year local-currency government bond yield, 22.31% (house cost-of-capital reference, cached 21-Jul-2026 print, re-verified 05-Aug-2026)

sov_spread_cds.source: Egypt CDS-implied sovereign default spread, Damodaran January-2026 country-premium file, CDS column. Netted out of the local-currency risk-free rate so sovereign default risk is not charged twice

sov_spread_rating.source: Damodaran adjusted default spread on the rating basis (Caa1), January-2026 — the alternative construction, disclosed for the audit trail

erp_cds.source: Damodaran original country-premium file, Egypt row, CDS column, last updated 5 January 2026 — total equity risk premium

erp_rating.source: Damodaran original country-premium file, Egypt row, rating basis, January-2026 — the alternative

erp_ops_weighted.source: Operations-weighted equity risk premium: 30% Egypt at 9.41% and 70% rest-of-world at a 6.5% blended emerging/frontier premium, reflecting where the revenue is actually earned. Shown as an explicit alternative, not the primary, because the standing house rule takes the country premium of the listing and reporting currency

beta.source: Own-stock tier-1 regression: SWDY weekly log-returns against a 31-name equal-weight EGX composite built from the full covered library, 5-year window. R-squared 0.291, n = 258, standard error 0.098, 90% confidence interval [0.85, 1.17]. Comfortably clears the usability gate and is NOT weak-instrument flagged (R-squared well above 10%, interval span 0.32 against a 1.009 point estimate)

kd.source: Marginal cost of debt, CURRENCY-BLENDED. The audited FY2024 interest-rate note discloses average rates on financial liabilities of 28.68% in Egyptian pounds, 6.49% in US dollars and 3.92% in euros, and Note 32 confirms 28.6% / 6.45% / 7.45%. The blended rate the company actually pays is far below the Egyptian rate because a majority of the book is hard currency. Set at 13.0% against the independently computed effective rates below, allowing for the CBE's easing since the FY2024 note

kd_egp_note.source: Average interest rate on Egyptian-pound financial liabilities, audited FY2024 interest-rate-risk note

kd_usd_note.source: Average interest rate on US-dollar financial liabilities, audited FY2024 interest-rate-risk note

kd_eur_note.source: Average interest rate on euro financial liabilities, audited FY2024 interest-rate-risk note

debt_open_fy24.source: Loans and credit facilities at 1 January 2024, financing-liability reconciliation, audited FY2024 note 32

debt_close_fy24.source: Loans and credit facilities at 31 December 2024, financing-liability reconciliation, audited FY2024 note 32 (excludes 286.1 of lease liabilities)

int_exp_fy24.source: Interest expense on loans and credit facilities, audited FY2024 note 32 financing-liability reconciliation

debt_q1_25.source: Loans and credit facilities at 31 March 2025: the FY2024 closing balance of 58,796.8 less the 3,646.9 net repayment shown in the Q1-2025 interim cash flow statement

kd_path.source: Forward cost-of-debt path FY26E-FY30E on the blended book. The Egyptian leg follows the CBE easing cycle (main operation rate 19.50%, held since April 2026 after three consecutive pauses) toward the 7% (2026) and 5% (2028) inflation targets; the hard-currency leg is broadly flat. The discount-rate glide takes its shape from this path by construction rather than being invented separately

kd_term.source: Terminal blended cost of debt: ~45% Egyptian pound at the 15% long-run Egyptian corporate-borrowing norm and ~55% hard currency at ~6.5%

rf_term.source: Terminal risk-free rate, norm-built: the CBE's own stated medium-term inflation target of 5% plus the standard ~5.5pp emerging-market real-rate convention. Never a raw historical average and never reverse-engineered from a price

erp_term.source: Terminal equity risk premium, normalised below the currently elevated crisis-era level toward the rating-class norm; never held flat into perpetuity

wd_term.source: Terminal debt weight D/(D+E), NORMALISED rather than today's weights. The company runs a gross debt book sized to fund working capital but carries very large offsetting cash, so its net leverage is light; 25% is the steady-state structure for a diversified industrial of this scale

g_term.source: Terminal growth, 5% — the standing centre for established names in this market post-disinflation, sensitised 3-7%. Note this is an EGP-NOMINAL rate struck against a terminal risk-free rate that itself embeds 5% inflation, so the base case assumes approximately zero real terminal growth: a deliberate conservatism for a company whose revenue is majority hard-currency

ev_ebitda_just.source: Justified EV/EBITDA on mid-cycle FY27E EBITDA. The company's own trailing multiple is ~7.9x; listed cable and electrical-equipment peers trade 8-11x and Riyadh Cables ~14x on earnings. 6.5x applies an Egyptian-market discount for sovereign, currency-convertibility and disclosure risk. Bear 5.5x / bull 8.0x

pe_just.source: Justified through-cycle P/E on normalised earnings. Trailing is ~13.0x. 9.0x reflects a high-quality franchise held back by an Egyptian cost of equity near 28%. Bear 7.0x / bull 11.5x

roe_sust.source: Sustainable return on equity for the book lens. Trailing ROE is ~27.5% on average parent equity; the FY2023-24 prints were flattered by devaluation inventory gains, so the sustainable rate is struck below them

lens_weights.source: DCF primary for an operating manufacturer with a long, contracted order book; the relative and normalised-earnings lenses carry equal secondary weight and the book lens least, because reported book value is distorted by three years of currency translation

backlog_usd_bn.source: Group project backlog approximately USD 6.5bn, above the group's typical historical range (company 2025 commentary)

ownership.source: CORRECTED. The company's own shareholder pie chart carries 78.18% / 20.37% / 1.45% against the legend 'El Sewedy Family / Free Float / Electra Investment Holding'. Reading that in legend order gives a 20.37% free float — which is wrong. Electra Investment Holding (Abu Dhabi, IHC-linked) acquired ~427.7mn shares, about 20%, in a July-2024 mandatory tender offer at USD 1.05/share (~USD 449mn), confirmed by multiple independent reports of the exchange filing. The 20.37% slice is therefore ELECTRA, not the float. Independent sources put the family near 68%, leaving a free float of roughly 11.6% — about half what a legend-order reading implies. Material to governance and to liquidity

electra_mto.source: Electra Investment Holding's mandatory tender offer, concluded July 2024: ~427.7mn shares (19.98%) at USD 1.05/share, ~USD 449mn, advised by EFG Hermes. Roughly EGP 50/share at the exchange rate then prevailing. Recorded as the last known price at which a strategic buyer cleared a fifth of the company. NOT used as a valuation anchor: it is two years stale, struck before the earnings base grew by roughly half, and at less than half today's price

dps_fy25.source: FY2025 dividend of EGP 1.85 per share (+85% on the FY2024 EGP 1.00), approved at the 6-May-2026 general meeting and paid from 4 June 2026 — i.e. BEFORE the anchor date. Roughly EGP 3.96bn. The study previously reported only the FY2024 distribution

e3.method_short: cash returns vs cost of capital

assert_log: SWDY — ASSERT / derivation log

[P&L closure FY2025] disclosed profit after tax 19,180 at the stated 25.0% effective rate implies pre-tax profit 25,573; less net finance -3,400 and associates 1,302 gives EBIT 27,671, and adding depreciation 2,951 gives EBITDA 30,622 (10.90% of revenue). The disclosed quarterly EBITDA margins were 12.6% (Q1), 11.1% (Q2) and 9.5% (Q4), so a full-year figure near 11% is consistent with the prints. NCI 1,850

[EBITDA basis] House EBITDA = operating profit + depreciation and amortisation: FY23 20,035, FY24 31,602. The company's own reported EBITDA (20,668 / 32,772) is higher because it also adds back impairments and certain other charges; the house basis is used throughout so the DCF waterfall reconciles line by line.
[Working capital] FY23 36,655 (24.1% of revenue), FY24 53,495 (23.1%), FY25 64,641 (23.0%, held at the historical level)

[FY2025 balance sheet triangulation] equity attributable 70,464 (FY24 55,275 + profit 17,330 - dividend 2,141); total equity 76,316; liabilities 234,774. Gross debt: (A) balance-sheet residual 76,166, (B) revenue-scaled 71,580, (C) implied by revenue-scaled cash 67,105 -> adopted 71,617, cash 51,828. NET debt is NOT triangulated — it is the disclosed 19,789, and the valuation bridge uses only that.

[Kd integrity] (i) CURRENCY COMPOSITION — audited note rates: EGP 28.68%, USD 6.49%, EUR 3.92%. The blended effective rate implies an Egyptian-pound share of 43.5% and a hard-currency share of 56.5%. A single-currency Kd would overstate the cost of debt by roughly 1,326bp.
[Kd integrity] (ii) INDEPENDENT EFFECTIVE RATES — FY2024 interest expense 7,707 / average loans and facilities 49,982 = 15.42%; Q1-2025 finance costs annualised / average balance = 12.26%.
[Kd integrity] (iii) BOUNDS — adopted Kd 13.00%: within 150bp of the most recent effective rate (74bp) and does not exceed the peak-year effective rate 15.42% by more than 50bp.

[Cost of equity] rf 22.31% less sovereign CDS spread 3.40% = 18.91%; + beta 1.009 x ERP 9.41% -> Ke 28.40%. Alternatives disclosed: rating basis 30.01%; operations-weighted premium 26.35%; the RETIRED un-netted construction 31.80% (audit trail only).

[WACC explicit] weights on NET debt 8.1% / equity 91.9% -> 26.90%. On gross debt the weights would be 24.1% / 75.9% -> 23.90%; the net-debt basis is used because it is the same quantity the enterprise-to-equity bridge subtracts, and it is the more conservative of the two.
[WACC terminal] Ke 17.56% (rf 10.50% + beta x ERP 7.00%); Kd after tax 7.88%; weights 75%/25% -> 15.14%

[Glide] forward WACC 26.90% -> 22.98% -> 19.55% -> 17.10% -> 15.14%; cumulative discount factors 0.7880, 0.6408, 0.5360, 0.4577, 0.3975. The glide fractions are the cost-of-debt path's own cumulative progress, so the shape is inherited rather than being a second free parameter.

[Bottom-up base] the sub-segment build reconciles to the audited statements: FY2023 revenue 152,186.2 vs reported 152,186.2, gross profit 29,077.5 vs 29,077.3; FY2024 revenue 231,981.9 vs 231,981.8, gross profit 43,898.4 vs 43,898.5.

[Unit economics] cables price/tonne 360,780 -> 522,361; fabrication uplift over copper 1.386 -> 1.261; conversion margin 25.0% -> 22.8%. Meters price/unit 1,748 -> 2,596; transformers price/MVA 455,485 -> 641,847. Operating load between gross profit and EBITDA 5.94% -> 5.30% of revenue.

[FY2025 unit base] volumes implied from the disclosed Q1 prints and the FY2024 seasonal share: cables 154,621t (-7.8% on FY2024), meters 5,550,494 units, transformers 17,516 MVA. Cables revenue is the residual against the disclosed group revenue of 281,049, which BACK-SOLVES the FY2025 fabrication uplift to 1.204, against 1.386 in FY2023 and 1.261 in FY2024. That this residual lands in the historical neighbourhood is the check that the segment split is economics rather than a plug — and it is the test that rejected the competing '+51% E&C' reading, which forces the uplift to 1.077.

[FY2025 margin calibration] cables gross profit is PINNED to the disclosed 88,173 EGP per tonne x 154,621t = 13,633, i.e. a conversion margin of 14.8% against 22.8% in FY2024 — the cable margin roughly HALVED, and that single fact is most of the group's gross-margin decline. The other lines carry FY2024's margins scaled by 0.804, solved so the total reproduces the 40,720 assembled from the disclosed prints. Resulting FY2025 margins: Cables 14.8%, Raw material (copper rod) 12.4%, Engineering & construction 9.0%, Transformers 27.7%, Meters & digital 21.9%, Other electrical products 40.8%, Infrastructure investment 49.7%.

[FY2025 operating load] bottom-up gross profit 40,720 less EBITDA 30,622 implies an operating load of 3.59% of revenue, against 5.30% in FY2024 and 5.94% in FY2023. The forecast glides from 4.0% back toward the historical norm rather than assuming the FY2025 level persists.

[Q1-2026 calibration] the disclosed Q1-2026 revenue 75,298 (+26.8% y/y) and attributable profit 4,845 (+16.8% y/y) imply, on the same tax, minority, finance and depreciation structure, an EBITDA margin of about 11.24% — against 12.61% in Q1-2025. Profit GREW on a higher copper price, so any build that shows margins collapsing in FY2026 is contradicted by the print. The FY2026 cable conversion margin is therefore SOLVED to reproduce this, not assumed.

[Per-unit gross profit, FY2025 base] cables 88,173 EGP/tonne (disclosed), rod 62,592 EGP/tonne, transformers 279,950 EGP/MVA, meters 655 EGP/unit. These grow with cost inflation only — no real recovery in conversion profitability is assumed anywhere in the forecast.

[Cable conversion margin, solved] FY2026 gross profit per tonne solves to 157,818 EGP to reproduce the Q1-2026 implied EBITDA margin — against the disclosed 88,173 in Q1-2025, 119,043 in FY2024 and 90,020 in FY2023. It sits inside the historical range, so the print and the unit build are mutually consistent.

[Conversion margin cross-check] as a SHARE of the realised price per tonne that solved figure is 17.8%, between the FY2025 trough of 14.8% and the FY2024 peak of 22.8%. In absolute EGP it is below what pure copper-cost scaling of FY2024 would give (196,336), so the solve does not assume the converter captures the whole metal move. NOTE the solve attributes all of the Q1-2026 improvement to cables, where the volatility demonstrably is; if it in fact came from another line the sub-segment split changes but GROUP EBITDA — the only thing the valuation consumes — is pinned by the print either way.

[FY2026 cross-check against the print] the disclosed Q1-2026 revenue of 75,298, grossed up on the Q1-2025 seasonal share, implies a full year of 356,321. The build produces 365,556, +2.6% against it — an independent check that the unit build is not running ahead of the company's own trading.

[Currency split — two different questions] the company discloses that over 70% of revenue is earned ABROAD, which is a geographic statement about where the customer sits. The build derives the share that is HARD-CURRENCY LINKED — dollar-priced by construction — at 63% in FY2025 and 62% -> 61% -> 61% -> 60% -> 60% thereafter. The two are not in conflict: a project executed in a North African market for a local utility is foreign revenue but not necessarily dollar-priced. The LOWER figure is used everywhere the currency question is valued, because it is the conservative one.

[Forecast interest] net finance cost falls 4,127 -> 4,311 -> 3,470 -> 2,321 -> 943 as the cash pile builds against a broadly static gross debt book — the charge tracks the net debt path rather than being frozen at the FY2025 balance.
[Forecast equity] attributable profit 23,403, 25,655, 28,761, 32,311, 36,224; net debt path 27,358, 23,957, 16,044, 5,129, -9,025 (25% payout assumed).
[Terminal return on capital] taken as next year's NOPAT over the closing invested capital (21.8%), the standard convention, rather than the same year's NOPAT over closing capital (20.8%).

[Terminal growth reconciliation] historical ROIC 22.3% / 24.9% / 20.9%; reinvestment rate 20.8% / 31.7% / 26.4%; implied g 4.6% / 7.9% / 5.5%. Check (a): actual NOPAT CAGR FY23-FY25 = +30.5%. Check (b): implied g from STABLE years only (FY24 excluded as a debt-funded capacity burst, reinvestment 32%) = 5.1%. Adopted terminal g 5.0%.

[Terminal value] terminal ROIC 21.8%; required reinvestment rate g/ROIC = 22.9%; terminal NOPAT 41,331; TV 314,122 capitalised at the terminal WACC and discounted at the YEAR-5 factor 0.3975 (one date, one price of time) -> PV 124,875. Terminal value is 77% of enterprise value.

[Terminal ceiling] the domestic leg is 40% of FY30E revenue; a blended long-run nominal ceiling is 10.5% (15% Egyptian nominal on the domestic leg, 7.5% world nominal on the export leg). Adopted g of 5% sits below it. If the recent NOPAT CAGR of 30% were floated as a TERMINAL rate, the domestic revenue leg alone would overtake Egypt's entire nominal GDP in about 36 years — arithmetic necessity, not a modelling opinion.

[Associates] carried at the audited FY2024 carrying value of 6,474 with NO uplift. The previous version applied an undisclosed 1.15x, which an external audit correctly flagged as an unsourced adjustment; it is removed.

[Bridge] EV 162,810 - net debt 19,789 + associates at carrying value 6,474 = 149,495; less minority interests at their 9.6% share of group profit = 14,419 -> equity attributable 135,075 = EGP 63.10/share against a spot of 105.20 (-40%).

[Currency-of-discounting alternative — UIP-corrected] the hard-currency leg (60% of cash flow) is first DEFLATED to dollars at each year's exchange rate, discounted at a USD cost of capital of 10.12% with 3.5% terminal growth, and only then translated back. Discounting the EGP-denominated leg — already inflated by the assumed depreciation path — directly at a dollar rate would count the currency benefit twice, which is what the previous version did. Corrected result EGP 91.15/share (-13% vs spot), against 108.27 before the correction.

[Rating-basis alternative, published] on Damodaran's RATING column (sovereign spread 6.37%, equity risk premium 13.94%) the cost of equity is 30.01% and the cost of capital 28.37% -> 18.55%, giving EGP 44.88/share against the CDS-basis 63.10. Both columns are published by the same source; the CDS basis is the house primary because it is market-observed rather than agency-lagged. The rating basis is now shown as a VALUE, not merely as a rate.

[EGP-equivalent cost of debt alternative, published] the pound has depreciated (and this forecast assumes it keeps depreciating) at 5.4% a year on average over the explicit window; loading that onto the hard-currency legs (56% of the book, coupon blend 5.21%) under uncovered interest parity gives an EGP-equivalent cost of 10.92% for that share, and a blended Kd of 18.65% against the currency-composition 13.00%. Cost of capital rises to 27.24% from 26.90%, giving EGP 62.69/share against 63.10. CAUTION: adopting the currency-composition Kd as primary — as this study does — means the hard-currency share of the debt book is carried at its coupon rate and NOT compensated for devaluation risk beyond what the forecast's own FX path already assumes; if the pound depreciates faster than that path, the true cost of servicing that debt in pounds is understated by this study's primary construction.

[Minority-interest sequencing, alternative published] charging minorities 9.6% of UNLEVERED enterprise value plus associates (16,328) and deducting net debt afterwards gives EGP 62.20/share, against 63.10 on the adopted sequencing — a difference of -0.89. The adopted method is retained because the audited borrowings note records facilities granted to 'the Company AND ITS SUBSIDIARIES ... guaranteed by promissory notes FROM SUBSIDIARIES', i.e. debt does sit at subsidiary level, so minorities do bear a share of it. The alternative assumes all borrowing is at the parent, which the note contradicts.

[Relative lens — forward EV discounted] 6.5x on FY2027E EBITDA 44,941 gives an enterprise value of 292,115 AS AT end-FY2027; discounted back at the year-2 factor 0.6408 that is 187,184 today -> EGP 73.38/share. Not discounting it would have given 117.67.

[Book lens] justified price-to-book 1.47x = (sustainable return 23.5% - growth 5%) / (PERPETUAL cost of equity 17.56% - growth). Using a blended cost of equity inside a perpetuity formula, as the previous version did, is inconsistent and understated this lens by roughly 14.61/share.
[DCF scenarios] bear 35.37 / base 63.10 / bull 110.39 EGP per share
[Synthesis] weighted central EGP 74.52; full span across lenses and scenarios 33.77 - 154.50; spot 105.20 (-29% to the central).
[Leverage] net debt / EBITDA falls from 0.65x to -0.16x over the forecast.

[Economic profit convention] the capital charge is taken on BEGINNING-of-year invested capital, not ending. Charging ending capital understates economic profit by roughly 3,832mn a year and pushes the year in which the return spread turns positive one year later than it should. Corrected here.
